subject: Agriculture
title: Permaculture Design
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Permaculture Design.

hook.text: Permaculture designs permanent agricultural systems that mimic natural ecosystems. Plant once, harvest indefinitely.

buildup.text: Bill Mollison and David Holmgren coined 'permaculture' in 1978—permanent agriculture using ecological design.

discovery.text: Zones radiate from the house—intensively managed gardens close by, orchards further, and wild areas at the edges.

twist.text: Permaculture works brilliantly for small homesteads but struggles to scale to commodity crop production.

climax.text: Its greatest influence is as a design philosophy—teaching farmers to think in systems rather than single crops.

punchline.text: Design a farm like a forest. Diverse, self-sustaining, and productive.

quiz.question: What is permaculture's core principle?
options: Design permanent systems that mimic natural ecosystems

details.summary: Permaculture is a design system for creating sustainable human settlements modeled on natural ecosystems. In agriculture, it applies principles like stacking functions, closing loops, and working with nature to design productive, self-maintaining food systems.
details.whyItMatters: Permaculture has inspired millions of people worldwide to redesign gardens, farms, and communities for resilience. Its principles of observation, integration, and minimal waste are increasingly relevant in an era of climate uncertainty.
takeaways: Permaculture designs productive systems modeled on natural ecosystem patterns
Core principles include stacking functions, closing nutrient loops, and using zones
Bill Mollison and David Holmgren developed permaculture in the 1970s in Australia

faq.question: What are the core design principles of permaculture?
faq.answer: Permaculture uses principles like observe and interact, catch and store energy, obtain a yield, produce no waste, use small and slow solutions, value diversity, and use edges. Everything serves multiple functions and waste from one element feeds another.

faq.question: How does permaculture apply to food production specifically?
faq.answer: Permaculture food systems include food forests (multi-layer tree and shrub systems), keyhole gardens, swales for water harvesting, companion planting guilds, and zone-based placement where frequently tended plants go nearest the home.
